title: Add a cache
hints: The answers are already right. What is missing is the two lines that use `memo`: one that looks, one that stores.
Look first: before the base case, write `if (r, c) in memo:` and return `memo[(r, c)]`.
Store before returning: after `answer` is worked out, write `memo[(r, c)] = answer`. The key is the tuple `(r, c)` because the answer depends on both numbers.

answer.explain: The reference checks `memo` for the key `(r, c)` before doing any work and returns the stored answer when it is there. Otherwise it works the answer out once, stores it under `(r, c)` and returns it. Each square is then worked out one time, so `paths(8, 8)` takes 129 calls where the starter takes 25739.
